title: Personal KPI weekly check-in - Samira Patel
content:
Weekly check-in (2026-03-01) - personal KPI / OKR draft and retrospective

Quick summary:
- Focus this sprint: reduce 95th P99 latency for small-chat models on Dedicated by improving batching heuristics and KV cache hit rate.
- Progress: prototyped adaptive batcher changes (local experiments), identified one regression in KV cache eviction.
- Blockers: need perf trace for segfault observed on node-7 when batch size > 16; infra slot to run longer stress test.

OKR/Goals (draft):
- OKR 1: Improve inference reliability and tail latency (team / personal contribution)
  - KR1: Reduce 95th-token latency for small-chat models on Dedicated from 310ms -> 230ms (measurable)
  - KR2: Reduce error rate for streaming connections > 30s from 0.8% -> 0.2%
  - KR3: Add rollout checks + automatic fallback for top 3 regions (canary -> full)
  - My actions: implement adaptive batching, add KV-cache instrumentation, own rollout playbook updates.

- OKR 2: Developer productivity improvements for model-ops
  - KR1: Cut average per-deploy rollback time from 18m -> 8m by improving tracing and runbook steps
  - KR2: Ship a lightweight local dev harness for model serving (alpha)
  - My actions: iterate on local harness README, get feedback from 3 SEs, write PR template.

This week: detailed notes / todo
- Monday: perf run local on model-x-large (seq=128), found P99 improvement of ~20ms after kernel tweak. Notes in PR: https://github.com/redwood/serving-runtime/pull/901 (TODO: add perf graphs).
- Tuesday: KV cache eviction seems aggressive for long-running chats; hypothesize a bug in LRU timestamp update path. Reproduce locally, stacktrace pinned to cache.c:118. File ticket ENG-542.
- Wednesday: paired with Avery on adaptive batcher; merged experimental feature branch (flag: batcher.adaptive=true). Ran smoke on Dedicated staging - noticed increased mem usage on some instances. Follow-ups: memory profiling.
- Thursday: wrote draft for rollout playbook (confluence link above), need product review from Ryan (assigned).
- Friday: retro notes (see below).

Retro / personal reflection:
- Wins: shipped prototype changes faster than expected by keeping scope narrow; got good feedback from SEs on harness UX.
- Learnings: I tend to over-optimize for throughput early; need to gate on reliable metrics first (more dashboards).
- What to stop: avoid carrying forward half-baked benchmarks into PR descriptions; instead attach a short checklist: "sanity run, perf graph, env details".
- What to start: 30-min async demo sessions for infra changes so SREs can provide early feedback.

Immediate next actions (week of 2026-03-02):
- Blocker: schedule node-7 repro window with infra and get core dump. Owner: Samira. Due: 2026-03-03.
- Add KV cache instrumentation (timestamps + hit/miss counters) and push to staging. Owner: Samira. Due: 2026-03-05.
- Memory profile adaptive batcher on 8 GPU nodes. Collaborators: Avery. Due: 2026-03-06.
- Update rollout playbook with canary metrics + rollback triggers; ask Ryan for review. Due: 2026-03-04.

Notes to self / loose ideas:
- Consider adding a small local HTTP shim that mimics Dedicated routing for testing fallback logic.
- Explore a lightweight tracing id propagation for prefix-cache hits across services.
- If batcher memory overhead persists, add configurable max-batcher-ram per node.

References and links:
- ENG-542 (KV cache eviction ticket)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood/serving-runtime/pull/901
- Confluence playbook draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/rolling-deploy-playbook
- Slack: #eng-runtime-weekly thread (search "batcher adaptive mem")

Open questions (for next sync):
1) Is the precedence of TTL vs. LRU eviction intended for persistent chat sessions? (ask SRE)
2) Should we prioritize rollout automation or improved tracing first for rollback speed?
3) What is acceptable memory overhead for adaptive batcher on Dedicated small instance types?

End of check-in. Quick personal rating: 7/10 - progress steady but want faster resolution on node repro and KV instrumentation.

-- Samira
